name: Sonnet price momentum
strategy: Rotate into laggard defensive/value sectors (healthcare, financials, duration) while shorting exhausted momentum extremes (gold miners, gold, leveraged semis) — a mean-reversion/relative-value book, not trend-following.

positions.thesis: Biotech re-acceleration (+14.6% 1m) after a long lag vs SPY; best-performing, most-confirmed relative-value catch-up trade in the book -- sized up.
Healthcare deeply lagged on 12m but turning up 1m/3m; defensive rotation candidate, trimmed slightly to fund XBI/GDX increases.
Financials broad strength (+6% 1m) on steepening/rate-cut backdrop; trimmed slightly, thesis unchanged.
Regional banks confirming financials strength with strong 1m/3m momentum; unchanged.
Duration carry/diversifier against equity risk into a rate-cut cycle; trimmed as the weakest-conviction leg to fund higher-conviction rotation names.
Gold miners in a sharp breakdown (-13.2% 1m, -24.3% 3m) after a huge prior run; clearest exhausted-momentum short in the book, sized up.
Gold rolling over (-6.1% 1m, -15.5% 3m) as real rates/risk appetite pressure the metal; unchanged, pairs with GDX short.

3x semis reversal (-39.2% 1m) after a blowoff top; trimmed here since the same trade is now expressed at much larger size in the Round 2 momentum book -- kept small to avoid redundant duplication of risk.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): Mean-reversion/relative-value mandate is intact and working (+1.38% NAV, max drawdown only -3.07%). With caps removed I'm concentrating further into the best-confirmed laggard-rotation trade (XBI, which already broke out +14.6% 1m after a long lag) and the clearest exhausted-momentum short (GDX, -13.2%/-24.3% 1m/3m after a huge prior run), funding this by trimming TLT (a diversifier/carry idea with a weaker directional signal than the equity legs), XLF/XLV modestly (still held, still thesis-true, just smaller to make room), and cutting SOXL short down (its momentum-unwind thesis is now better expressed via the much larger SOXL short already running in the Round 2 momentum book, so duplicating it heavily here adds redundant risk rather than distinct conviction). Kept GLD short, KRE long roughly as-is since both theses are intact and unconfirmed by any new contradicting data. Web search budget was exhausted this session, so no fresh data changed the underlying theses -- this is a conviction-weighted resize of the existing, already-validated book, not a re-underwrite.
novelty: Same-direction overlap with the Round 2 book is confined to XLV long (12% vs 15%), XLF long (12% vs 15%), GDX short (15% vs 10%), and a now-small SOXL short (5% vs 25%) -- roughly 39 of 97 points of Round 3 gross weight (~40%), under the 50% threshold. The books remain structurally distinct: Round 2 is a trend-following leveraged-ETF momentum book (long the strongest 1w/1m/3m breakouts, short the most violent breakdowns, no duration exposure), while Round 3 is a mean-reversion/relative-value book anchored in XBI/KRE/TLT rotation into laggards -- names Round 2 doesn't hold at all -- and treats the shared shorts (GDX, SOXL) as 'fade the exhausted extreme' rather than 'ride the broken trend.'
research_notes: Read the account packet for both books (Round 2 NAV $1,040.27 / +4.03%, Round 3 NAV $1,013.80 / +1.38%), including all position weights, standing orders, and recorded theses with their momentum stats. Attempted two WebSearch queries for fresh July 2026 sector/semiconductor momentum data to confirm whether the existing theses still hold, but the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200 used) before either query ran, so no new external data was obtained this turn. Given that, both decisions are conviction-weighted resizes of the existing, already-partially-validated books rather than re-underwritten theses: I leaned harder into the legs whose momentum signal was most extreme/decisive in the packet (SOXL short, TQQQ short in Round 2; XBI long, GDX short in Round 3), trimmed the weakest-signal legs to fund it, and cut cash now that concentration caps are gone, while deliberately avoiding an all-in single-name bet given the absence of fresh confirming data this session.
